title: Configuring Virtual Service Edge for Internet & SaaS and NTP Server Synchronization

blocks.text: Virtual Service Edges for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) are extremely sensitive to the virtual machine (VM) and cloud times being in sync. By default, the Virtual Service Edges synchronize their time with public NTP servers (pool.ntp.org) when the Virtual Service Edge services start. However, if you have a local NTP server, you can configure the Virtual Service Edges to synchronize time with it.
You can enable the NTP daemon (ntpd) to synchronize its time, using your local NTP servers or pool.ntp.org, with the following command:
vzen ntp-manager

blocks.item: The commands vzen enable-ntpd, vzen disable-ntpd, and vzen modify-ntpd-servers are deprecated and replaced by vzen ntp-manager.

Modifying the NTP configuration causes the Virtual Service Edge services to stop and restart. This restart takes several minutes longer than a standard restart due to NTP synchronization. Ensure that you apply NTP changes during a maintenance window and that the Virtual Service Edge management interface can reach your NTP servers over UDP port 123.

blocks.text: For the first-time deployment, configure the Virtual Service Edge to use either your local NTP servers or the public servers.

Apply the changes immediately by entering y. Zscaler recommends applying the changes immediately.

blocks.text: Alternatively, you can configure the public servers (pool.ntp.org).
To configure the Virtual Service Edge to use public servers:

blocks.item: Log in to the Virtual Service Edge.
Press Enter at the server prompt.
Apply the changes immediately by entering y. Zscaler recommends applying the changes immediately.
Your servers are the preferred time sources. The public servers (pool.ntp.org) are kept as a fallback.

For Virtual Service Edges deployed on VMware ESXi, ensure that the ESXi host's clock is synchronized with NTP and that the Synchronize guest time with host option is disabled in the VM's VMware Tools settings.

blocks.text: To check the NTP server status, run the following command:
sudo vzen ntp-manager --status
See image.
The output shows whether ntpd is running and its time is synchronized, and lists your configured servers.
Synchronization can take a few minutes after the first start.

blocks.text: Disabling NTP stops the ntpd, and the Virtual Service Edges synchronize their time with public servers (pool.ntp.org) when services start. If the Virtual Service Edges cannot reach the public servers, their time might drift. The configured server list is preserved, allowing you to re-enable NTP later.

blocks.text: If you configured NTP on an existing deployment, standardize the NTP configuration on all the Virtual Service Edges with vzen ntp-manager.
To see the steps that apply to your node, run the following command:
sudo vzen ntp-manager --validate
See image.
If the validation fails, follow the steps shown in the output or contact Zscaler Support.
